newsitem.title: UK: Britain considering bugging prison cells - paper.
newsitem.headline: Britain considering bugging prison cells - paper.

text.p: British Home Secretary (interior minister) Michael Howard has secretly approved a plan to bug prison cells to help solve major crimes, a newspaper said on Monday.
"The aim is to catch some of the country's most dangerous criminals boasting about their exploits -- or setting up new crimes," The Daily Mail, a popular tabloid, said.
The Home Office (interior ministry) refused to confirm the report. "It is not something we would discuss," a spokesman told Reuters.

The newspaper said details of the bugging plan, which would target murderers, sex offenders and armed robbers, were understood to have emerged in documents disclosed to the lawyer defending a man facing further proceedings after being taped.

It is part of the ruling Conservatives' plan to get tough on crime, an issue which is sure to emerge in the campaign leading up to the next general election in seven months. The ruling Conservative are trailing the opposition Labour Party by 20 points in opinion polls.

The Daily Mail added that some prison guards are so concerned about the alleged plan, which is aimed at providing new leads on criminal cases, that they have written to the Prison Officer's Association.

"This has been kept very secret, but we are concerned about the legal position and the relationship between prisoners and prison officers which we have worked hard to build," the newspaper quoted a letter from prison guards as saying.
Civil liberty groups described bugging as an invasion of privacy. They also questioned whether such information would be admissible in court.
